premises.text: Doctors make bad decisions because reference tools ignore clinical experience and there is no structured way to share experience with peers
premises.evidence_span: Good doctors, like me and Mark, wind up making bad decisions because we have no way to share our experience

premises.text: SharePractice ranks treatments by doctor votes with clinically relevant dosing and peer comments so doctors can decide and contribute in seconds
premises.evidence_span: these treatments are actually ranked by doctors upvoting and downvoting these treatments

premises.text: A viral invite flow shares a structured treatment question to doctor contacts and pulls new users into the reference tool
premises.evidence_span: Share Practice generates the email for you

premises.text: A proprietary medical ontology unifies messy medical terminology across databases so collaboration stays coherent
premises.evidence_span: SharePractice built a proprietary medical ontology that took multiple databases

premises.text: The platform collects unique why-this-treatment data valuable in a large analytics market
premises.evidence_span: we're getting data that doesn't exist anywhere

value.text: Patients get better treatment because doctors carry collective peer experience in their pocket
value.evidence_span: share practice puts a million doctors in every doctor's pocket

secondary_value.text: Unique why-prescribed analytics data for the analytics market
secondary_value.evidence_span: we're getting important information on the most valuable customer in a $10 billion analytics market

causal_links.evidence_span: we have no way to share our experience
you're going to get the best treatment

notes: Reference-tool inadequacy and peer-texting pain folded as one experience-sharing problem (§4.1.6). Ranking/dosing/comments cascade folded into the reference product; viral share split as GTM/growth mechanism baked into product. Ontology kept as separately claimed feasibility condition. Global collaboration vision partly as value. Anti-template: problem, clinical product+ontology, and analytics data separately revisable.
